thread:
Alex: Heads-up: noticed a big p99 regression on API generation endpoints right after the debug-span rollout at 09:12. p99 token latency jumped from ~280ms to ~980ms in prod. Anyone else seeing this?
Priya: Yup seeing it. Grafana shows a ~3x increase in otel_span_received_total and CPU for otel-collector pods spiked to 85%.
Mateo: Any chance the new instrumentation is emitting huge spans (attachments/large attrs)? I saw a few spans with ~50KB attrs in the staging traces.
Alex: Confirmed. New debug middleware added `request_body` and `response_body` as span attributes for some routes. We shipped it behind a flag but the flag defaulted to on for prod accidentally.
Sam: ops-bot shows deploy 2026-03-17T09:10 (commit 9f3b2a). Rolling back might be fastest if needed. But want to diagnose cause before rollback.
ops-bot: deploy: service=api-gateway env=prod commit=9f3b2a status=success time=2026-03-17T09:10:23Z
Jing: Two quick angles: 1) exporter batching config could be too small causing more frequent network sends -> higher CPU and latency. 2) span volume increase -> more KV cache thrash in runtime.
Priya: Query from Prometheus: `sum(rate(otel_span_received_total[1m])) by (service)` shows api-gateway from 600/s -> 1800/s around 09:12. Also `sum(rate(otel_collector_exporter_sent_spans_total[1m]))` matches.
Mateo: Also observed increased `otel_collector_exporter_batch_duration_seconds` p99. Looks like batching windows are hitting timeouts instead of filling, so more flushes.
Alex: Current collector config snippet (from k8s secret):
```yaml
service:
  pipelines:
    traces:
      receivers: [otlp]
      processors: [batch, memory_limiter]
      exporters: [otlp/internala]
processors:
  batch:
    send_batch_size: 200
    timeout: 200ms
```
Priya: send_batch_size 200 + timeout 200ms + 3x span rate -> means more flush cycles. Try increasing send_batch_size to 1000 and timeout to 500ms as an experiment. Also compress gRPC export (gzip) to reduce CPU on network serialization?
Jing: Compression moves CPU from network into CPU too. But it can reduce network pressure and maybe reduce number of exporter calls. We should profile which side is heavier.
Sam: Can we change processor ordering to run a brief sampling/attr-scrub before batch to drop large attrs? E.g., a custom sampling processor to drop `request_body` for responses > 10KB.
Mateo: We have `attributes` processor; can add `actions: - delete: request_body when: size_gt(10240)` — quick hack. But that requires collector restart/rolling update.
Alex: For quick mitigation I propose: 1) flip flag off for debug spans (rollback of feature flag) 2) increase batch size to 1000 and timeout 500ms 3) add attributes delete rule in staging and run for 30m before prod. Thoughts?
Priya: +1. Let's do flag off first to stop immediate pressure. Then batching change to reduce flush frequency; that should lower p99 quickly.
Jing: I'll prepare a k8s patch for collector config and an attributes rule. Ping me when flag is off so I can roll.
Sam: I'll flip the feature flag to off in LaunchDarkly now and post status.
ops-bot: feature-flag: debug-spans for env=prod set to OFF by Sam at 2026-03-17T09:23:45Z
Sam: Flag is off. Traffic should stop producing those large attrs in ~10s.
Priya: Metrics: otel_span_received_total dropped back to ~650/s within 40s. Collector CPU trending down to 38% now. p99 token latency back to ~320ms. Looks much better. :thumbsup:
Alex: Great. Next actions: Jing applies batching+attr deletion in canary for 10% of collectors, monitor for 1 hour, then rollout. Also add a follow-up task to change default flag to off and add unit tests preventing default-on for debug flags.
Mateo: Also we should consider dynamic sampling in the collector tied to route and response size — keep full spans for errors and sampled for normal responses. I'll draft an RFC.
Priya: Can we add a quick alert rule: if otel_collector_cpu > 70% && otel_span_rate > 2x baseline for 5m -> page oncall. We almost missed this pattern because only latency alerted.
Alex: Good idea. Sam, can you add that alert?
Sam: On it. Creating alert ticket and will create a pager duty rule.
Jing: Patch ready for batching/attr delete; I'll wait 10m and then apply canary to cluster `telemetry-prod-canary`.
Alex: Thanks all. Please paste postmortem blurb into #postmortems when we have final timeline.
Priya: TL;DR for postmortem: accidental default-on debug spans increased span volume and attribute sizes leading to frequent exporter flushes; root cause: feature flag default and lack of size-based attr scrubbing in collector. Remediations: revert flag default, batching tuning, add attribute scrubbing, dynamic sampling RFC, and alert rule.
Mateo: I'll attach a flamegraph of collector CPU once we finish the canary so we can show where time was going.
Alex: Closing thread after canary verification. Thanks!
